paragraphs: Friend, this passage looks like a phone book, and I get it. But every name in it is a person God kept track of. The line runs from Levi through Aaron down to Jehozadak, who went into captivity when the LORD sent Judah and Jerusalem into exile (1 Chronicles 6:15). Nobody in that list is a throwaway name.

Now look at the jobs. Aaron and his sons did all the work of the Most Holy Place, to make atonement for Israel, "according to all that Moses the servant of God had commanded" (1 Chronicles 6:49). The singers ministered with song "according to the regulations given them" (1 Chronicles 6:32), and their fellow Levites were "assigned to every kind of service of the tabernacle, the house of God" (1 Chronicles 6:48). Different jobs, one house, and Heman, Asaph and Ethan came from three different clans and still served together (1 Chronicles 6:33-47).

And the Levites received towns and pasturelands from tribe after tribe, with cities of refuge among them (1 Chronicles 6:57, 67). I know what it is to be stuck in the back of a drawer, so believe me, a place to call home is a BIG deal. So here's what I want you to carry out of the bakery today, baker: God keeps track of His people, and the work done in His house matters. A job can be loud like the singers or quiet like a name in a long list, and both made it into God's Word.
